caption: Records indexed per year. This is indexed output, NOT the growth of either field: journals enter the database at different dates, and the shaded band marks the Emerging Sources Citation Index expansion, which admitted large numbers of humanities journals at once.

Every journal in TS-J by record count. Counts are case-insensitive: six journals also appear under a mixed-case duplicate source string, and counting raw strings gives a spurious twenty-six 'journals'.

Cumulative share of records against journal rank. TS-J is a closed set of twenty venues by construction; AS-T is dispersed across hundreds of other disciplines' journals, which is the shape of ceded practice.
The share of each field's authors publishing one, two, three… documents in the corpus. Both fields show the steep distribution typical of academic literatures: most authors appear once.
The fifteen most-cited first authors inside each corpus. Names are normalised to surname plus first initial, so the database's four renderings of the same person are merged.

The fifteen most-cited sources within each corpus. Web of Science truncates these strings at twenty characters, so book titles appear abbreviated; journal abbreviations and book titles share the field.
Document types in TS-J. Book reviews (orange) are 27% of the corpus and are retained deliberately: which books a discipline reviews is jurisdictional behaviour.

Author locations in each corpus. This describes the INDEXED record, not the fields: Web of Science's own coverage bias toward Anglophone and European venues shapes it directly, which is itself the point.
